Subject: Intro + MAP request: cost checks ahead of pilot

Hi David —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Pacemed is excited to move toward a short pilot but procurement needs a simple mutual action plan (MAP) and a cost sanity check before we lock dates. Two things we specifically need from Redwood for the MAP package:

- A short evaluation plan (key success metrics, what we’ll measure during the 4-week pilot).
- Unit economics assumptions (tokens/$ baseline, expected cache hit, batching assumptions, and an ops checklist showing where cost can swing).

We don’t need a perfect model — just enough to validate we’re not off by an order of magnitude before legal/procurement start redlines. We expect ~150k monthly active users in scope for the pilot (conversational triage flows), but can share a traffic histogram if helpful.

Procurement timeline: vendor review opens 09/16; ideal to have MAP + cost notes by 09/15 to avoid blocking.

Thanks — can you send a draft MAP and a short units-per-dollar workup? I can loop in our finance lead if you want detailed traffic.

—Olivia

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>

Olivia —

Thanks — attaching a MAP draft and the quick tokens/$ model for an initial sanity pass. High-level notes here so procurement can get a first-order view immediately:

Attachment summary:
- pacemed_map_draft.xlsx (MAP tasks, milestones, success criteria, tentative dates)
- token_econ_model_v2.csv (line-item units-per-dollar scenarios: hosted baseline, quantized hosted, dedicated GPUs)

Key baseline assumptions in the spreadsheet (explicit so you can tweak):
- Average prompt tokens per request: 120 tokens (includes system + user).
- Average completion tokens per request: 220 tokens.
- Requests per active user (pilot): 3 per day average.
- Cache hit rate (prefix/KV cache): 30% (moderate reuse of templates).
- Effective batching window: 8 requests (we assume continuous batching for throughput ops).
- Units-per-dollar baseline (hosted curated model): ~3,200 tokens / $1 (equivalent to $0.3125 per 1k tokens).

Illustrative math (hosted baseline):
- Monthly tokens = users * daily requests * (prompt + completion) * 30 days = 150k * 3 * 340 * 30 ≈ 4.59e9 tokens/month.
- With 30% cache, effective billed tokens ≈ 3.21e9 tokens/month.
- At 3,200 tokens/$ => ~ $1,003k/month.

That delta is large (six figures), so the model includes quick scenarios: raise cache to 50% (prefetch/pinned templates), batching gains (improve throughput and reduce concurrency premium), or run a quantized dedicated model (approx 2x units/$ improvement in our conservative estimate).

Next steps I propose:
1) Laura — quick finance sanity check on our baseline units/$ assumptions and whether we should present a hosted vs dedicated comparison for procurement.
2) Olivia — if you can send a traffic histogram by tomorrow, I’ll re-run the model with realistic P95 request sizes.
3) Rishi — can you confirm the batching/caching feasibility and any latency tradeoffs we should call out for the MAP ops checklist?

Goal: ship a one-page MAP appendix with a 3-scenario cost table by Tue 09/15.

Attachment: pacemed_map_draft.xlsx (xlsx, 42 KB)
Attachment: token_econ_model_v2.csv (csv, 18 KB)

Best,
David Kim
Head of GTM Finance, Redwood Inference

David / Olivia —

Quick notes from finance review of the CSV and MAP draft:
- Units-per-dollar baseline looks aligned with our current hosted public model but we should avoid presenting a single-point estimate. Procurement likes a named-hosted vs quantified-dedicated breakout.
- Please add: effective hardware assumption for the dedicated scenario (e.g., A100x2 equivalent, expected model quantization level: int8 vs int4) — that drives the 1.8–2.5x gap in tokens/$.
- Call out one-off engineering migration costs (prefetching integration + KV cache policy) vs ongoing per-token delta. Procurement will ask total cost of ownership for the pilot window.
- For the MAP appendix please include a sensitivity table: +/- 20% on average completion length and +/- 10% on cache hit. That usually closes early procurement questions.

I can help format a compact 1-page cost appendix for the MAP if you want me to redline the spreadsheet.

—Laura

Looping in engineering notes on batching/caching feasibility for the MAP appendix:

- Batching: we can safely batch up to 8–12 requests in the steady-state path without violating a 400ms generation SLO for short responses. For longer completions the batching window increases latency; we’ll call out latency bands in the appendix.
- Prefetch / KV caching: given 45% templated flows, prefix caching can realistically achieve 30–55% hit depending on template granularity. We will instrument a quick AB test during the first week of pilot to measure actual hit rate.
- Billing semantics: even with caching active, some providers bill per generated token — our MAP table shows both raw token count and billed token estimate after cache. Make sure procurement sees the billed number.
- Dedicated vs hosted: dedicated model (quantized int8) is feasible for the timeline (pilot start +2 weeks) but requires a short ops switch plan (we’ll include a 3-step canary: 1) shadow traffic, 2) 10% traffic on dedicated, 3) full cutover). Ops cost to stand-up dedicated nodes is included in the CSV as a one-time delta.

Action items:
- David: produce final 1-page appendix with 3 scenarios (hosted baseline, cached-hosted, dedicated-quantized) and include sensitivity +/-20% token sizes and +/-10–20% cache.
- Laura: redline financial language and confirm the procurement-facing phrasing for committed vs consumption pricing.
- Olivia: confirm pilot start target (earliest client-side readiness date) so we can present a realistic canary timeline.

I’ll be available for a 30-minute sync Tue morning if helpful.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Engineer, Inference Platform, Redwood Inference
